nodes.label: OptiAI
nodes.rationale: An AI optimizer built on routing logic extracted from 9Router v0.5.75: extracted backend layer + thin OptiAI API + a nine-tab product UI. Supports 16 enterprise providers (147 chat models) with real validated credentials.

nodes.label: 9Router v0.5.75 (upstream)
nodes.rationale: Upstream routing product whose engine OptiAI vendors. Its dashboard, auth, CLI launcher, MITM proxy and tunnels are deliberately not imported.

nodes.label: Extracted 9Router Backend Tree (422 files)
nodes.rationale: Kept near byte-identical under backend/9router so relative imports keep working, the extraction map stays 1:1, and upstream fixes re-sync as a file copy rather than a merge.

nodes.label: Upstream Path Preservation
nodes.rationale: Exact upstream paths are kept so (1) relative imports inside the tree work untouched, (2) docs/9router-extraction.md stays a 1:1 map, (3) re-syncing an upstream fix is a file copy, not a merge. Only 6 files differ, each marked with an '// OptiAI:' comment.

nodes.label: OptiAI HTTP API (backend/api/index.js)
nodes.rationale: Thin by design: every OptiAI route lives here but the logic lives in services/, which is the ONLY caller of backend/9router/.

nodes.label: OptiAI Service Layer (backend/services)
nodes.rationale: Declared the only caller of backend/9router/, so the vendored tree has exactly one seam to the product.

nodes.label: gateway.js Express-WHATWG Bridge
nodes.rationale: Bridges Express to WHATWG Request/Response so 9Router's Next-style handleChat runs unmodified with streaming intact - avoiding any edit to the vendored tree.

nodes.label: Node Alias Resolver Hook (server/hooks.mjs)
nodes.rationale: Teaches plain Node the '@/*' and 'open-sse/*' aliases 9Router relies on; loaded by register.mjs via node --import. Without it nothing in backend/9router resolves.

nodes.label: src/sse/handlers/chat.js - Pipeline Entry
nodes.rationale: App-side entry to the routing engine: API-key gate, combo expansion, account-selection fallback loop.

nodes.label: open-sse/handlers/chatCore.js
nodes.rationale: The routing spine: format detection, RTK, translation, executor dispatch, refresh-and-retry, streaming.

nodes.label: RTK Token-Saving Engine
nodes.rationale: 11 deterministic filters plus autodetect, caveman, ponytail and system-prompt injection. Savings are reported in bytes, not tokens, because real token deltas are only knowable from provider-reported usage.

nodes.label: pricing.js - Single Cost Formula
nodes.rationale: Model + provider + pattern pricing and cost math live in exactly one place; explicitly never to be duplicated in the frontend.

nodes.label: usageRepo - Usage and Cost Persistence
nodes.rationale: Writes per-request usage rows, daily rollups and cost at write time, so cost is fixed at the moment of the request rather than recomputed later.

nodes.label: OptiAI Request Flow
nodes.rationale: frontend -> /api/chat -> gateway.js -> sse/handlers/chat.js -> chatCore.js -> executor -> provider -> SSE back -> usage + cost written to SQLite.

nodes.label: backend/config/providers.js - 16-Provider Allowlist
nodes.rationale: Single source of truth for the narrowing. Every catalog, model and auth route filters through it, so anything outside the 16 404s. The 123 registry files stay on disk because registry/index.js imports every one, and the repo is not under version control, so a physical delete would be unrecoverable. Adding a provider back is one line in the allowlist.

nodes.label: Exclusion of Consumer-Subscription Providers
nodes.rationale: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Kiro, Antigravity, Windsurf, Trae, Zed etc. are excluded because they proxy a consumer subscription or an IDE OAuth session; 9Router itself ships them behind an 'account may be restricted or banned' notice, which rules them out for company use however well they work.

nodes.label: 16 Supported Enterprise Providers
nodes.rationale: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, Google Vertex AI, Azure OpenAI, xAI, Mistral, Cohere, DeepSeek, Groq, Cerebras, Together AI, Fireworks AI, Perplexity, OpenRouter, NVIDIA NIM - all reached with a licensed API credential; xAI is dual-mode (API key or OAuth), Azure models are your own deployment names.

nodes.label: Provider Connection Flow (API key / OAuth)
nodes.rationale: Keys are validated against the live provider before being stored, so a rejected key is never saved. Credentials are never environment variables - they are per-connection rows in the database.

nodes.label: Pasted OAuth Callback URL
nodes.rationale: The callback is pasted rather than captured because 9Router's loopback listener binds inside the backend process, where a browser tab cannot reach it.

nodes.label: Serial-First Model Testing
nodes.rationale: Test models sends a real 1-token completion through the full pipeline and colours each tile by result. The first model is tested alone so any OAuth refresh settles before the rest fan out, otherwise concurrent calls race on the same refresh token. These are billable requests but the only honest way to know a model works.

nodes.label: DATA_DIR Isolation from 9Router Install
nodes.rationale: OptiAI stores data in backend/.data, separate from %APPDATA%/9router, so it never touches existing data. First run is empty on purpose. To inherit connections, point DATA_DIR at a COPY - sharing the directory makes both apps write the same file.

nodes.label: Webpack Dev Server Over Turbopack
nodes.rationale: Turbopack's manifest writes race Windows Defender's real-time scanner on this repo (EPERM rename in .next/dev), so the dev script runs 'next dev --webpack'. dev:turbo opts back in only with a Defender exclusion. Symptom when it hits: the first route loads, then every subsequent route 500s with a missing /_error entry in build-manifest.json.

nodes.label: Root-Only npm Workspaces Install
nodes.rationale: npm install must run from the repo root: with --prefix, npm installs the root package into the child and adds a bogus "optiai": "file:.." dependency.

nodes.label: Logo-Derived Colour System
nodes.rationale: Colour comes only from the logo: Symbol.png's blue-violet gradient endpoints were sampled (#1F79FC -> #9642FD, body #8E55FB) into the brand/accent ramps. Components use semantic tokens (--surface, --text-muted, --brand), never a raw ramp step, so light/dark is one place to change.

nodes.label: frontend/src/app/globals.css - Design Tokens
nodes.rationale: The single source of colour in the product; brand ramps sampled from the logo with semantic tokens on top - change light/dark here and nowhere else.

nodes.label: Hand-Rolled SVG Charts (No Chart Library)
nodes.rationale: AreaChart, BarList and Gauge are hand-rolled SVG because a charting dependency would add ~90KB and its own theming layer fighting these CSS variables.

nodes.label: Screens Declare Unbacked Data In Place
nodes.rationale: Screens not backed by an endpoint say so in place; nothing renders invented numbers, and every screen holding state only in localStorage declares it on the screen itself.

nodes.label: frontend/src/lib/nav.ts - Sidebar Definition
nodes.rationale: Defines the nine sidebar tabs; 'expandable: true' is what makes Chat reveal its thread list inline. The rail is nav only - no New chat button or search box.

nodes.label: frontend/src/lib/api.ts - Typed Backend Client
nodes.rationale: Typed client for every backend route, including the SSE reader for /api/chat.

nodes.label: frontend/src/lib/analytics.ts - Score Derivation
nodes.rationale: Turns usage rollups into the three Analytics scores client-side; designed as the one module to swap when a real /api/analytics endpoint lands, keeping the layout.

nodes.label: Analytics as Deterministic Heuristic
nodes.rationale: Efficiency, Model Fit and Prompt Craft (0-100 gauges) are computed client-side from the same usage rollups the Usage tab reads, so the two pages can never disagree, and no model call is made.

nodes.label: useModelCatalog Hook
nodes.rationale: Aggregates models across providers without making 119 round trips.

nodes.label: Chat / Ask Mode Switch
nodes.rationale: Ask has OptiAI rewrite the prompt, name missing context and say what class of model it needs - but it sends a rewrite instruction to the selected model rather than running a dedicated optimizer, because no OptiAI prompt optimizer exists in this build. Every answer carries a telemetry footer: model, tokens, cost, latency.

nodes.label: Browser-Held State Limitation
nodes.rationale: Chat threads, projects, combos, per-model selection, custom model ids and round-robin live in localStorage because the backend has no table or route for them. combosRepo has full CRUD but nothing calls it; round-robin strategies exist in src/sse/services/auth.js but no route writes the setting they read.

nodes.label: /api/chat Auto-Attached Local API Key
nodes.rationale: The imported requireApiKey gate defaults to on and OptiAI has no app-level auth yet, so /api/chat attaches a stored local key rather than disabling the gate; the public /v1 gateway still enforces it normally.

nodes.label: AI Search Falls Back to Keyword Filtering
nodes.rationale: The search bars on Models and Skills are wired to the UI but fall back to keyword filtering, and say so, because reasoning over the catalog needs a connected provider.

nodes.label: MCP Bridge Deferred
nodes.rationale: OptiAI's skills/plugins system is treated as a new feature rather than a port of 9Router's MCP bridge, so the bridge is deferred, not merely excluded.

nodes.label: Curated Skill Library (static catalog)
nodes.rationale: Arbitrary Git repositories cannot be installed - a repo becomes available only once OptiAI adds it to lib/catalog/skills.ts.

nodes.label: CLI Gateway Integration
nodes.rationale: Issues gateway API keys and returns per-tool PowerShell/CMD/bash snippets plus a smoke test, but never edits ~/.claude/settings.json - config writing is deliberately not implemented.

nodes.label: canonicalizeUsage Preserves estimated Flag
nodes.rationale: Upstream dropped the estimated flag, making guessed (chars/4) token counts indistinguishable from provider-reported ones; OptiAI restores it so its analyzer never treats a guess as a measurement. Usage endpoints expose it as tokenSource provenance.

nodes.label: Quota Readers Extracted But Unexposed
nodes.rationale: open-sse/services/usage/* works, but no route surfaces it and no budget-aware selector exists yet; it was kept for future quota-aware tiering.

nodes.label: Backend Environment Variables
nodes.rationale: HOST stays on loopback because this process holds provider credentials. API_KEY_SECRET and MACHINE_ID_SALT ship insecure defaults; changing API_KEY_SECRET invalidates existing issued gateway keys. Provider credentials are deliberately not env vars.
